summary: Creates open or closed arcs, circles, and ellipses as primitive, polygon, NURBS, or Bezier curve geometry.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Primitive type: Primitive, Polygon, NURBS Curve, or Bezier Curve

key_params.name: orient
key_params.note: Circle plane: XY, YZ, or ZX

key_params.name: modifybounds
key_params.note: Modify input-derived bounds when an input is connected

key_params.name: order
key_params.note: Spline order for NURBS or Bezier curves

key_params.name: arc
key_params.note: Closed, open arc, closed arc, or sliced arc mode

key_params.name: imperfect
key_params.note: Use imperfect non-rational NURBS/Bezier circle approximation

common_gotchas: Primitive type is not recommended for instancing; use polygon or curve types when instance compatibility matters.
Unequal X/Y radii on non-rational NURBS circles can produce unexpected isoparms when skinned.
For skinning two circles, start from the same circle and transform one copy to keep compatible knot structure.
Arc angle can exceed 360 degrees and open/closed arc modes produce different point counts.
ZX orientation normals changed in build 2021.10000 to point along positive Y.
key_concepts: Circle SOP creates open or closed arcs, circles, and ellipses as primitive, polygon, NURBS, or Bezier geometry.
Primitive type controls which options are meaningful and whether the output suits instancing or downstream spline work.
Orientation selects the construction plane, while radius, translation, anchor, and arc controls shape the result.
Imperfect non-rational curves can avoid certain NURBS ellipse skinning artifacts but are approximations.
